cards.title: Read, understand, respond
sections: Reading

On Monday morning, Elena reads the new plan at work. She is a senior analyst, and her job is to check the numbers before the team meets. The first part of the plan is clear, and the ideas are easy to follow. But one number on page two is not precise. Elena calls Marcus, her colleague, and says, 'To my mind, the plan needs more time.' Marcus listens. He says there was a subtle change in the cost, and he did not show it well. Elena says, 'In essence, the plan is about trust. To put it another way, the numbers must be exact, or the team will not trust the plan.' Marcus agrees. He works on the numbers in the afternoon and gives Elena a precise number before the meeting. Elena reads the new number and smiles. She says, 'Thank you, Marcus. Now the plan is clear. A precise number helps the whole team.'

What does Elena say about the plan?
Write
Write a short email to a colleague. Ask for a precise number in their plan. Say why the exact number matters.

sections: Reading

He asks, 'To put it bluntly, do you think the plan will fail?' Elena says, 'No. I think the plan is sound, but we need one more week.' She says the report is explicit about the cost, and that part is clear. But the promise in it is only implicit, and the team may miss it. Marcus says, 'Thank you. A forthright answer helps me more than a kind one.' He works on the report in the afternoon. He makes the promise explicit, and he writes the date in clear words. On Thursday, he shows the new report to Elena. She reads it and says, 'Good. Now the work is clear. A forthright answer helped us both.' Marcus is glad to hear it.

/l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/ə/: Relax the tongue in the center.
/k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/e/: Start with the tongue mid-front.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/ʃ/: Tongue blade just behind the ridge; air flows.
/ə/: Relax the tongue in the center.
/n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.

Marcus says, 'You are right. I may understate the risk, too. The plan is not perfect.' Elena says, 'On the whole, your idea is coherent and easy to follow.' She says the first part is clear, and the last part is strong. Marcus is glad. Marcus listens with care. He does not want to sound proud. He says, 'Thank you. So we keep the idea and check the numbers first.' They check the numbers together in the afternoon. The numbers are sound, and the plan is clear. Elena says, 'Good.
